scope.summary: mcp/binding.rs::atomic_replace publishes the discovery binding with a hand-rolled MoveFileExW that receives raw encode_wide() paths - no verbatim prefix, no GetFullPathNameW - while every neighbouring operation on the SAME path goes through Rust std::fs, which normalizes. At a CWD-relative length of 260 the rename fails with ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND after the temp file has already been created, hardened, written and fsynced.

defect_detail.site: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/binding.rs, atomic_replace Windows branch lines 424-449; error surfaced at 454-458; wrapped into "MCP discovery binding was not safely published" at mcp/server.rs:163-168.
defect_detail.measured_empirically: A purpose-built non-longPathAware Win32 probe (GetFileAttributesW) measured the exact boundary with CWD set to the crate root: 259 chars resolves, 260 and 261 return err=3. The temp name is swarm_mcp_binding.{pid}.{19-digit-nanos}.tmp, so a 5-digit PID lands on exactly 260.
defect_detail.reproduced_from_the_real_failing_run: The failing run left its PID in an artifact path: handshake-test/native_gui/pid-69592/frames/block_collection_view_screenshot-pid69592-1.png, mtime 2026-08-13 00:21:34, matching the lock created at 00:21:54. PID 69592 is five digits; reconstructing its exact temp filename and probing it returns err=3, while the 235-char destination .json resolves fine. The reported os error 3 was reproduced exactly, from the real PID.
defect_detail.why_the_message_misleads: The error names the 235-char DESTINATION, which is perfectly valid. The 260-char SOURCE is what Win32 rejected. Anyone reading the message looks at the wrong path.
defect_detail.manifest_checked_not_assumed: The test binary carries NO embedded manifest at all - searched for manifestVersion / longPathAware / RT_MANIFEST in ASCII and UTF-16, all absent, with pwsh.exe as a positive control. Machine-wide LongPathsEnabled=1 therefore cannot rescue it.
defect_detail.the_stale_lock_theory_is_REFUTED: A repo-wide census of Handshake_Artifacts found ~48 binding roots, 42 of which carry a .lock with no .json. That is the by-design resting state: binding.rs:294-296 declares the lock persistent and remove_binding (:582-586) deletes only the .json. The lock carries ZERO diagnostic signal. A swarm_mcp_binding.lock.stale-preserved-20260812 file exists in exactly one root - evidence an earlier agent chased this red herring. The advisory OS lock is released automatically when its process dies, so no age or PID breaker is missing.
defect_detail.why_only_this_one_binary_fails: Every other Argus test installs ScopedArgusAppData (canonical_argus_driver.rs:49-58), which CANONICALIZES the root to absolute - 196 chars, always safe. test_block_collection_view.rs:2491 deliberately passes app_data: None and keeps the ../../../../ relative fallback root from :2080-2083. That single difference is why it is the only red binary of its class.

acceptance_criteria.AC-129-1: Both MoveFileExW operands are resolved through GetFullPathNameW and given the Win32 verbatim prefix before the call, so the publish path tolerates any length std::fs tolerates.
acceptance_criteria.AC-129-2: Proven RED first: a test that publishes a binding under a root long enough to exceed 260 fails before the fix and passes after. A fix with no RED is not accepted.
acceptance_criteria.AC-129-3: The failure message names the operand that actually failed. Naming the valid destination while the source is what Win32 rejected cost this packet a full diagnostic cycle.
acceptance_criteria.AC-129-4: test_block_collection_view passes WITHOUT HANDSHAKE_ARGUS_BINDING_ROOT set - i.e. on the relative fallback root that currently breaks it. That is the real acceptance surface; the env var is a workaround, not a fix.

proof_targets.PT-129-1: The RED run for AC-129-2, output retained.

scope.risk_if_missed: This is not test-only. binding_path() resolves under %LOCALAPPDATA%; any operator whose profile path is deep enough hits the same failure in the shipped app, and the published error blames a path that is fine.
scope.secondary_risk_found_in_passing: test_block_collection_view.rs:2089 sets the process-global LOCALAPPDATA with no guard and no mutex, while pg_proof_support/mod.rs:3989-3991 documents that this variable requires NATIVE_BINDING_ENV_LOCK because two suites in one binary would otherwise authenticate against each other binding root. It is safe only under --test-threads=1. Under default parallelism it will race ScopedArgusAppData install/drop - which recursively removes its root - and produce a GENUINE missing-directory os error 3 with a message identical to this defect.

lifecycle.creation_reason: Isolated while unblocking MT-116 AC-116-3. MT-116 own recorded hypothesis (a creation race in the binding publisher) is wrong, and so is the stale-lock theory. Confirmed by reproducing the exact os error 3 from the real failing run PID. Unrelated to MT-116 chip-rendering change, so filed separately rather than absorbed.

implementation_result.ac_129_1: MET. Both MoveFileExW operands go to Win32 in extended-length (verbatim) form via a local verbatim_wide helper that canonicalizes to absolute first, so a caller-supplied relative root behaves the same as an absolute one. UNC paths take the UNC verbatim form.
implementation_result.ac_129_2: MET, and this is what makes the fix credible rather than plausible. A new lib test, write_binding_survives_a_root_past_the_legacy_max_path_limit, publishes a binding under a root padded past the limit. With the fix reverted it fails with the EXACT production error shape (replace ... atomically); with the fix restored it passes. binding lib tests 14 passed / 0 failed.
implementation_result.ac_129_3: MET. The error named only the destination, which during the real failure was the 235-character path that was FINE while the 260-character source was what Win32 rejected. It now names both operands with their character counts.
implementation_result.ac_129_4: MET, on the REAL acceptance surface rather than the workaround. test_block_collection_view is 29 passed / 0 failed with HANDSHAKE_ARGUS_BINDING_ROOT UNSET - on the relative fallback root that previously broke it. The env var is no longer required.
implementation_result.not_test_only: binding_path() resolves under the local app-data root, so an operator with a deep enough profile hit this in the shipped app, and the published error blamed a path that was fine.
implementation_result.secondary_risk_NOT_addressed: The unguarded process-global LOCALAPPDATA set at test_block_collection_view.rs:2089 is untouched. It is safe only under --test-threads=1 and can still race ScopedArgusAppData under default parallelism, producing a GENUINE missing-directory os error 3 with a message identical to this defect. Stated rather than silently folded in; it is outside this MT scope.
implementation_result.validation_boundary: KERNEL_BUILDER issues NO PASS verdict. Implementation evidence only.

hbr_obligations.MAN: UserManual must record that the discovery binding root should be absolute and short until this is fixed.
hbr_obligations.INT: HBR-INT-009: Flight Recorder NOT_APPLICABLE (local file publish); internal_diagnostics and Palmistry DEFERRED-with-reason per CX-981-005.
